title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, administered tracers and agents
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Methods that need an administered tracer or agent: PET, magnetic particle imaging, magnetoelectric nanoparticles, contrast-agent ultrasound and gas-vesicle reporters. 10 papers. Status: mixed. Functional magnetic particle imaging reaches 0.04-0.9 times BOLD sensitivity (approved tracers at the low end); magnetoelectric nanoparticle routes fail their budgets in physical models. Contrast-agent ultrasound and gas-vesicle reporters are placed here as administered agents. In public FDG-PET data a 64-s activation component was null (p=0.49), but in 9 adults visual-cortex FDG uptake rose too early in 10-min blocks for phosphorylation alone (p=0.004-0.008 across 8 variants), so a fast transport-like component is needed.
